question:
Given $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $AX=B$, where $B=\begin{bmatrix}7 & 4\\5 & 3\end{bmatrix}$:

(a) Show that $A$ is invertible and find $A^{-1}$.

(b) Determine the matrix $X$ using $X=A^{-1}B$.

(c) Verify the result by calculating $AX$.
explanation:
(a)
$$|A|=2(1)-1(1)=1\neq0$$
Therefore, $A$ is invertible.
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{1}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$

(b)
Since $AX=B$, multiply both sides on the left by $A^{-1}$:
$$X=A^{-1}B$$
$$X=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7 & 4\\5 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
$$X=\begin{bmatrix}7-5 & 4-3\\-7+10 & -4+6\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$

(c)
$$AX=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
$$AX=\begin{bmatrix}7 & 4\\5 & 3\end{bmatrix}=B$$
Hence, $X=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\3 & 2\end{bmatrix}$ is verified.

options.D:
(a) $|A|=0$, so $A^{-1}$ does not exist
(b) $X$ cannot be uniquely determined
(c) $AX=B$ cannot be verified
